title: Markup written directly into the document ({lang})
description: The script writes markup with {sink}. The string is parsed as HTML in the current document, so any interpolated value becomes markup — including an event handler or a script element that the original page never contained.
remediation: Build nodes with the DOM API and assign text, for example {safe}, so values are never parsed as markup.
limitation: Lexical, line-based: matches the write without tracing the interpolated value.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on direct document writes in {lang} code.
fp: A constant markup fragment with no interpolation is the common false positive.
recordDesc: In {lang}, {sink} hands the string to the HTML parser. Interpolation is the whole risk: the parser does not distinguish developer text from a request value.
applicability: Legacy front-end code, third-party widgets and analytics snippets.
risk: Script execution in the page that issues authenticated requests; MEDIUM severity.
fix: Create nodes and set text content ({safe}).
If markup is required, sanitise it with an allowlist.
verifyT: Rescan shows no direct document write carrying interpolated data.

title: XML document loaded with external entities enabled ({lang})
description: The code loads a document with {sink} without disabling DTD processing. An XML input can then declare an external entity that reads a local file or an internal URL, and the parsed value carries the content back to the caller.
remediation: Load with DTD processing disabled and a resolver that refuses external resources, for example {safe}.
limitation: Lexical, line-based: matches the load without inspecting the reader settings.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on XML document loads in {lang} code.
fp: Loading a document the service itself generated, with no external input, is the common false positive.
recordDesc: In {lang}, {sink} applies the default reader settings. Those defaults historically allow DTDs, which is the whole mechanism behind an entity-expansion or file-read attack.
applicability: Import endpoints, SOAP clients and configuration loaders in .NET.
risk: Local file disclosure and server-side request forgery through entity expansion; MEDIUM severity.
why: {lang} leaves DTD handling on by default ({sink}).
fix: Disable DTD processing and set a null resolver ({safe}).
Reject documents that declare a DOCTYPE.
verifyT: Rescan shows XML loads with DTD processing disabled.

title: Constructor selected by name at runtime ({lang})
description: The code obtains a constructor through {sink}. The class and constructor are chosen from strings at runtime, so a value that reaches them instantiates a type the application never intended to create.
remediation: Keep constructor lookup on constant types and an allowlist, for example {safe}.
limitation: Lexical, line-based: matches the lookup without tracing the class name.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on reflective constructor lookup in {lang} code.
fp: Dependency-injection frameworks that instantiate a fixed class name are the common false positive.
recordDesc: In {lang}, {sink} turns a string into a constructor. Application code that passes a request value into the lookup lets the caller choose what gets built — often a class with side effects in its constructor.
applicability: Plugin loaders, deserialisation helpers and generic mappers in Java.
risk: Instantiation of unintended classes with attacker-controlled state; MEDIUM severity.
fix: Use an allowlist of permitted classes ({safe}).
Prefer a factory with an explicit mapping.
verifyT: Rescan shows constructor lookups restricted to an allowlist.

java:ctor: a factory with an explicit class map

title: String split advances a caller-owned cursor ({lang})
description: The code splits with {sink}, which advances a pointer the caller owns. A nested loop that reuses the same cursor consumes the outer iteration's remaining input, and the bug shows up as missing fields, not as an error.
remediation: Keep one cursor per parse, or copy the segment before splitting it, for example {safe}.
limitation: Lexical, line-based: matches the call without tracking cursor ownership.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on cursor-based tokenisation in {lang} code.
fp: A parse that finishes before the next begins is the common false positive.
recordDesc: In {lang}, {sink} mutates the pointer passed to it. Reusing that pointer for a second, nested split silently truncates the first.
applicability: Protocol header parsing and CSV handling in C.
risk: Fields parsed from the wrong offset, which can mis-assign a value to a security-relevant field; LOW severity.
why: {lang} advances the caller's cursor in place ({sink}).
fix: Copy the segment before a nested split ({safe}).
Keep a separate cursor per parse level.
verifyT: Rescan shows nested parses using independent cursors.

c:strsep: a copy of the segment for a nested parse

title: Secret read from the environment in Go ({lang})
description: The code reads a credential from the environment with {sink}. Environment values are inherited by every child process and appear in process listings and dumps, so the secret outlives the code that needed it.
remediation: Load the secret from a restricted file or manager, for example {safe}, and keep it out of the environment.
limitation: Lexical, line-based: matches the read without knowing whether the value is a secret.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on environment reads in {lang} code.
fp: Reading a non-sensitive setting such as a port or a log level is the common false positive.
recordDesc: In {lang}, {sink} copies the whole environment into the process. Anything the service starts inherits the same secret.
applicability: Containerised Go services that inject credentials as environment variables.
risk: Credential disclosure through child processes and host tooling; LOW severity.
why: {lang} environment values are inherited and inspectable ({sink}).
fix: Read the secret from a restricted source ({safe}).
Clear the variable after the client is built.
verifyT: Rescan shows secrets loaded outside the environment.

go:env: a 0600 secret file or a secret manager
